From b2840e33127ce0eea880504b7f133e780f567a9b Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Date: Wed, 25 Feb 2026 11:59:58 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] btrfs: add missing RCU unlock in error path in
 try_release_subpage_extent_buffer()

Call rcu_read_lock() before exiting the loop in
try_release_subpage_extent_buffer() because there is a rcu_read_unlock()
call past the loop.

This has been detected by the Clang thread-safety analyzer.

Fixes: ad580dfa388f ("btrfs: fix subpage deadlock in try_release_subpage_extent_buffer()")
CC: stable@vger.kernel.org # 6.18+
Reviewed-by: Qu Wenruo <wqu@suse.com>
Reviewed-by: Boris Burkov <boris@bur.io>
Signed-off-by: Bart Van Assche <bvanassche@acm.org>
Reviewed-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>
Signed-off-by: David Sterba <dsterba@suse.com>

diff --git a/fs/btrfs/extent_io.c b/fs/btrfs/extent_io.c
index 3df399dc8856..051309e90079 100644
--- a/fs/btrfs/extent_io.c
+++ b/fs/btrfs/extent_io.c
@@ -4494,6 +4494,7 @@ static int try_release_subpage_extent_buffer(struct folio *folio)
 		 */
 		if (!test_and_clear_bit(EXTENT_BUFFER_TREE_REF, &eb->bflags)) {
 			spin_unlock(&eb->refs_lock);
+			rcu_read_lock();
 			break;
 		}
 
-- 
2.34.1

## Summary of Modifications

### File: `fs/btrfs/extent_io.c`

- **Change**: Added a missing `rcu_read_lock()` call in the function `try_release_subpage_extent_buffer()`.
- **Location**: Inside the loop, within an error path where the code breaks out because the `EXTENT_BUFFER_TREE_REF` bit is already clear. Prior to this fix, the code only released the spin lock (`spin_unlock`) but did not acquire the RCU read lock before breaking. However, after the loop exits, there is a corresponding `rcu_read_unlock()` call. This led to an unbalanced RCU lock/unlock (the unlock would correspond to no matching lock), detected by the Clang thread-safety analyzer.
- **Fix**: Insert `rcu_read_lock();` immediately after `spin_unlock(&eb->refs_lock);` and before `break;` in that specific branch.

### Relationship

The modification is isolated to a single file and a single conditional block. Its purpose is to ensure proper RCU locking symmetry: every `rcu_read_unlock()` call that follows the loop must be paired with a prior `rcu_read_lock()`. The missing lock in one exit path of the loop caused an underflow of the RCU read-side lock counter, potentially triggering lockdep warnings or improper behavior. The patch restores the expected pairing without affecting any other logic.
